task_3.title: Surface invalid warning payloads in pytest.warns
task_3.description: The update changes pytest's warning assertion behavior so invalid uses of warnings.warn are no longer silently accepted inside pytest.warns(). Instead, pytest now validates that warning payloads are valid warning messages and raises a type error for unsupported values, preventing confusing or misleading passes during warning assertions.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `pytest.warns()` does not hide invalid `warnings.warn()` calls. If code under a `pytest.warns()` context emits a warning with a payload that is neither a string message nor a `Warning` instance, the misuse should surface as a `TypeError` instead of being treated as a successful warning match.

expectation.grounded: `pytest.warns()` must validate captured warnings against the public contract of `warnings.warn()`, accepting string messages and `Warning` instances. If a warning captured within the context resolves to the default `UserWarning` form with a non-string first argument, `pytest.warns()` should raise `TypeError` rather than silently accepting it as a matching warning. Existing matching behavior for valid warnings should remain intact.
expectation.conceptual: `pytest.warns()` should fail fast on invalid warning payloads instead of masking them. Valid warning emissions should continue to work normally, while invalid payload types should be rejected with a type error so users see the real misuse.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the successful behavior of `pytest.warns()` for warnings emitted with a string message or a `Warning` instance. Do not reject explicitly constructed warning objects solely because they are subclasses other than `UserWarning`. Avoid introducing new failure conditions for valid warnings that were already supported by `warnings.warn()`.
constraints.conceptual: Keep valid warning assertions working as before. Only the previously hidden misuse of unsupported warning payload types should start failing.

behavior: `pytest.warns()` now validates whether warnings emitted inside its scope come from a valid `warnings.warn()` payload.
If code under `pytest.warns()` emits a warning using an unsupported non-string, non-`Warning` payload that becomes a default `UserWarning`, the context manager raises `TypeError`.
Warnings emitted with standard string messages remain accepted and are matched normally by `pytest.warns()`.
Warnings emitted as explicit `Warning` instances remain accepted and are matched normally by `pytest.warns()`.
The change makes invalid warning payloads fail consistently during warning assertions instead of being obscured by pytest's warning-capture machinery.
acceptance_criteria: When code inside `pytest.warns(...)` calls `warnings.warn()` with a string message, it should continue to be captured and matched without raising a type error.
When code inside `pytest.warns(...)` calls `warnings.warn()` with a `Warning` instance, it should continue to be captured and matched without raising a type error.
When code inside `pytest.warns(...)` calls `warnings.warn()` with a payload that is neither a string nor a `Warning` instance, `pytest.warns(...)` should raise `TypeError` instead of passing.
When an invalid warning payload would previously have been hidden by `pytest.warns(...)`, the failure should now be visible as a type error during execution of the warning assertion.

task_2.title: Add independent test-case verbosity control
task_2.description: Pytest now supports configuring test case execution verbosity separately from the main verbosity level through `verbosity_test_cases`, allowing collection and run output to be made more or less detailed without changing other verbosity-driven behaviors.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest users can control the verbosity of test case collection and execution output independently from the global verbosity level by using `verbosity_test_cases`, so terminal reporting can be tuned without changing unrelated verbosity behavior.

expectation.grounded: Pytest should accept the `verbosity_test_cases` configuration option and use it as the effective verbosity for test case reporting in normal runs and `--collect-only` output. This setting should determine whether terminal output shows only compact progress symbols, file-oriented progress, or one line per test case with outcome words; it should also determine whether long skip reasons are shortened or shown in full and whether collected-item docstrings/details are included.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to make test execution and collection output quieter or more detailed without changing the overall application verbosity. Increasing the dedicated test-case verbosity should reveal more per-test information, while lowering it should keep output compact.

constraints.grounded: If `verbosity_test_cases` is not explicitly set, existing verbosity behavior should continue through the normal fallback to the main verbosity level. The new setting should affect only test case collection and execution reporting, including file-path visibility, long test information, progress formatting, skip-reason detail, and collected-item detail; it must not change which tests are collected or executed, or alter assertion-specific verbosity controls.
constraints.conceptual: Changing this setting should only change how much detail pytest shows about collected and executed test cases. It must not change test outcomes, selection, or unrelated output categories.

behavior: Pytest exposes a dedicated `verbosity_test_cases` configuration option for fine-grained control over test case reporting verbosity.

During test execution, test-case verbosity values less than or equal to 0 keep progress-style output compact, while values greater than 0 switch to per-test reporting with full test identifiers and outcome words.
At test-case verbosity 0, progress output includes file-oriented context; at negative values, output is reduced to compact progress symbols without that higher-detail context.
When a skipped or xfailed test is shown in per-test reporting mode, test-case verbosity values below 2 shorten long reasons, while values of 2 or higher allow the full reason detail to be displayed.

In `--collect-only` mode, negative test-case verbosity emits compact collected-item output, values below -1 summarize by file counts, non-negative values show the collection tree, and positive values include additional item detail such as docstrings when available.
Visibility of long test information and related test-case display detail is governed by `verbosity_test_cases` rather than the global verbosity setting.
acceptance_criteria: When a project sets `verbosity_test_cases` without changing the main verbosity level, pytest should change test case reporting detail according to that setting while leaving unrelated verbosity behavior unchanged.

When `verbosity_test_cases` is greater than 0 during a normal test run, pytest should report each executed test case individually with a descriptive outcome label instead of only compact progress symbols.
When `verbosity_test_cases` is 0 or negative during a normal test run, pytest should keep execution output compact rather than printing one descriptive line per test case.
When a skipped test has a long reason and `verbosity_test_cases` is 1, pytest should abbreviate the displayed reason; when the value is 2 or higher, pytest should display the full reason detail.

When pytest runs with `--collect-only`, changing `verbosity_test_cases` should control whether collected tests are shown as a compact listing, file-count summary, or hierarchical collection tree with additional detail.
When `verbosity_test_cases` is not configured, pytest should preserve the prior behavior of deriving test case reporting detail from the main verbosity level.

task_1.title: Adopt pytest 8.1.1 importlib and namespace-package import behavior
task_1.description: Pytest 8.1.1 adds an opt-in setting for namespace-package-aware module resolution and changes importlib-mode collection so installed packages, src-layout projects, and conftest files are imported under the correct module identity when possible, while preserving fallback behavior for non-package paths.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to pytest 8.1.1 preserves correct collection and import behavior for test modules, doctest modules, and conftest files when using importlib-based importing, including src-layout and installed-package workflows, with optional support for namespace packages.

expectation.grounded: Pytest must expose the `consider_namespace_packages` ini option as a boolean configuration value defaulting to `False`. When this option is enabled, module name resolution used during `import_path()` for collected modules and `conftest.py` imports must treat namespace packages as valid package hierarchies. In `ImportMode.importlib`, pytest should first import a target by its resolved canonical package/module name when that target is reachable through normal import discovery, reuse the existing module object if it is already loaded, and fall back to a root-anchored standalone module name only when package resolution or canonical import is not possible. Initial `conftest.py` discovery must be based on the pytest invocation directory, and loading multiple non-package `conftest.py` files must not incorrectly reuse a previously cached `conftest` module.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should let projects opt into namespace-package-aware importing without changing default behavior. In importlib mode, pytest should prefer the real package identity of importable modules, especially for installed packages and src-layout projects, while still collecting files outside importable package roots through a safe fallback. Conftest discovery should follow where pytest was invoked from, and separate conftest files should remain isolated from each other.

constraints.grounded: Keep `consider_namespace_packages` disabled by default so existing package resolution semantics remain unchanged unless explicitly enabled. Preserve import-by-path fallback for files that do not resolve to an importable package/module name. Do not let `confcutdir` semantics block unrelated out-of-tree package hierarchies during conftest loading, and do not substitute a different same-named module for the requested file path when canonical resolution is unavailable.
constraints.conceptual: Default upgrade behavior should stay backward-compatible unless the new namespace-package option is turned on. Non-package files must still be importable by path, and isolation boundaries for conftest discovery should remain intact without breaking installed or externally located package trees.

behavior: A new boolean ini option, `consider_namespace_packages`, controls whether pytest treats namespace packages as part of module-name resolution during collection and import.

When importlib mode can resolve a collected file to a canonical package/module name, pytest imports it using that package identity instead of forcing a synthetic name derived only from the collection root.
If the canonical module is already present in `sys.modules`, pytest reuses the existing module object instead of importing the same module again under another identity.
If a file cannot be resolved as an importable package member, pytest still imports it from the requested path using fallback naming anchored to the collection root.
Conftest loading now resolves startup anchors and `confcutdir` relative to the pytest invocation directory rather than the ambient current working directory.
Multiple non-package `conftest.py` files no longer collide through a shared top-level `conftest` module cache during import.
acceptance_criteria: When a project enables `consider_namespace_packages = true` and collects a module that belongs to a namespace package reachable from `sys.path`, pytest should import that module under its canonical dotted package name.

When pytest runs with `--import-mode=importlib` against an installed package or src-layout package that is importable normally, collected modules and doctest modules should use the package's real module identity instead of a synthetic name based only on the repository root.
When pytest collects a file that is not reachable as part of an importable package, it should still import and collect that file successfully via its path-based fallback behavior.
When the same importable module is encountered again during the run, pytest should reuse the already loaded module rather than creating a second module object under a different name.
When pytest is invoked from a specific directory, initial `conftest.py` discovery and `confcutdir` handling should be evaluated relative to that invocation directory.

When separate non-package `conftest.py` files are loaded from different directories, each should be imported as its own conftest module without being replaced by another directory's cached `conftest`.

task_4.title: Fix path-based --override-ini handling without a config file
task_4.description: Pytest should no longer crash when path-valued ini options are provided through --override-ini in runs that do not have a discovered configuration file. Relative path values should keep using the config file directory when one exists, and otherwise use the directory where pytest was invoked.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest accepts path-valued --override-ini settings, including pythonpath, during invocations that do not have a discovered configuration file, and resolves relative values from the pytest invocation directory instead of failing during startup.

expectation.grounded: When pytest parses --override-ini for ini options of type paths or pathlist, including pythonpath, it should resolve relative entries against Config.inipath.parent when a configuration file is present, and against the invocation directory when no configuration file was found. The override should be applied during startup without raising AssertionError, and early root/config discovery plus initial conftest loading should use the invocation directory consistently in no-config scenarios.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to supply relative path-based configuration overrides on the command line even in projects that do not have a pytest config file. Those paths should be interpreted from the directory where pytest was started, and pytest should continue initialization normally.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing relative-path behavior for paths and pathlist ini values when a config file exists by continuing to resolve them from the config file location. Do not regress explicit config-driven startup behavior such as rootdir selection, conftest discovery, or override application by introducing failures when no inipath is available.
constraints.conceptual: Fix the no-config crash without changing the established behavior of projects that already rely on config-file-relative path settings, and keep startup/config discovery behavior predictable across invocation styles.

behavior: Path-valued ini overrides supplied through --override-ini are interpreted relative to the config file directory when pytest has a discovered configuration file.
If pytest is started without a discovered configuration file, relative values for path-valued ini overrides are interpreted relative to the directory where pytest was invoked.
Using --override-ini with pythonpath or other path-based ini options in a no-config invocation no longer aborts startup with an AssertionError.
In invocations without a config file, early root/config resolution and initial conftest discovery use the invocation directory as their reference point for relative paths.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest is launched from a directory that has no discovered pytest configuration file and is given --override-ini for a path-valued option such as pythonpath=src, it should start normally and honor the override.

When a relative value is supplied through --override-ini for a paths or pathlist setting and no configuration file is present, pytest should interpret that value relative to the directory from which pytest was invoked.
When a configuration file is present, relative values for paths or pathlist settings should continue to be interpreted relative to that configuration file.

When pytest performs early startup discovery without a configuration file, relative command-line anchors and conftest search boundaries should behave consistently with the invocation directory as the base location.

task_6.title: Add lazy bottom-up pytest node parent traversal
task_6.description: Pytest 8.1.1 adds a public node traversal helper that lets plugins and integrations iterate from the current node up through its parents without building and reversing a full ancestry list, while preserving the existing root-to-current ordering contract of listchain() and nearest-parent lookup behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to pytest 8.1.1 exposes a node ancestry API that supports bottom-up parent traversal from the current node to the collection root without changing existing ancestry ordering or nearest-parent resolution behavior.

expectation.grounded: The upgrade should provide pytest.nodes.Node.iter_parents() as a public helper that returns an iterator over the current node and each successive parent up to the root. The traversal order must start at self and move upward. pytest.nodes.Node.listchain() must continue to return the full ancestry as a list ordered from the root down to the current node. Ancestor-dependent node APIs such as Node.getparent() and marker iteration should preserve closest-first upward traversal semantics.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, consumers should be able to walk a collected pytest node's ancestry lazily from the node itself toward the root, while all pre-existing APIs that expose the ancestry as a root-to-leaf chain or resolve the nearest matching ancestor continue to behave the same way.

constraints.grounded: This change is additive: it must not remove or repurpose Node.listchain(), must not invert its ordering, and must not skip the current node when traversing parents. Parent lookup by type must still return the closest matching node, including self when applicable. Ancestry-based marker discovery must continue to observe nearer nodes before farther ancestors.
constraints.conceptual: The new traversal capability must not break existing plugin behavior. Code that relies on the old chain ordering or nearest-ancestor lookup should continue to see the same observable results, with the new API simply offering a more direct way to iterate upward.

behavior: A new pytest node helper, Node.iter_parents(), is available for iterating over a node and its parents lazily.
Node.iter_parents() yields nodes in bottom-up order, starting with the current node and ending at the collection root.
Node.listchain() remains available and continues to return the ancestry in top-down order from root to the current node.
Node.getparent(cls) continues to resolve the closest matching ancestor by searching from the current node upward.
Ancestry-driven marker traversal continues to evaluate markers on nearer nodes before markers on more distant ancestors.
acceptance_criteria: When a plugin or extension calls Node.iter_parents() on any collected node, it should receive an iterator that yields the current node first and then each parent in order until the root node is reached.
When code calls Node.listchain() after the upgrade, it should still receive a list containing the same ancestry ordered from the root node to the current node.
When Node.getparent(SomeNodeType) is called, it should still return the nearest matching node in the current node's ancestry, including the current node itself if it matches.
When node marker APIs enumerate markers across ancestry, markers defined on the current node or closer ancestors should still be observed before those from more distant ancestors.

task_5.title: Prefer canonical imports in pytest importlib mode
task_5.description: Pytest 8.1.1 changes --import-mode=importlib so it first imports modules through the normal package resolution path, without modifying sys.path, and only falls back to path-derived standalone imports when necessary. This fixes incorrect module naming and import failures for installed packages, src-layout projects, doctest collection, and namespace-package setups.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest importlib-based collection imports package code under its real package identity when possible, so installed packages, src-layout projects, doctest discovery, and namespace-package code do not fail or behave inconsistently because modules are loaded under path-derived names.

expectation.grounded: When pytest resolves a module path with --import-mode=importlib, it should first attempt to derive the canonical module name from the package layout and import it through the standard import mechanism without changing sys.path. Canonical-name resolution should honor the consider_namespace_packages setting for namespace packages. If the resolved canonical or fallback synthetic module name is already present in sys.modules, pytest should reuse that module object instead of importing it again. Only when canonical resolution or import is not possible should pytest import the file directly under a synthetic name derived from its path.
expectation.conceptual: Importlib mode should behave like normal Python imports for package code whenever the target module is importable, while still supporting direct collection of standalone files that are outside the import path. Users should observe stable module identities, fewer import mismatches, and correct behavior for doctests and installed-package layouts.

constraints.grounded: ImportMode.importlib must continue to avoid mutating sys.path. Existing prepend and append import modes must keep their current behavior. Direct-path fallback imports must remain available for modules that are not importable by canonical name, and generated fallback names must stay valid and unambiguous even when path components contain periods. Package-root resolution must not treat directories containing __init__.py as namespace-package boundaries.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must improve package-aware importing without changing the overall contract of importlib mode or breaking collection of standalone test modules. It should preserve compatibility with normal packages, namespace packages, and duplicate file names in different non-importable locations.

behavior: Pytest importlib mode now tries the standard package import path first for a discovered module, instead of always assigning a name from the file system path.
Installed modules that are reachable through the active Python import path are imported under their canonical package names rather than site-packages-derived or root-relative synthetic names.
If consider_namespace_packages is enabled, package root resolution extends across namespace-package segments so namespace-qualified module names are preserved during import.

If canonical package resolution fails or the module is not importable through the standard mechanism, pytest falls back to importing the target file directly under a synthetic module name derived from the path.
Repeated imports of the same canonical or fallback module name reuse the existing sys.modules entry instead of re-executing the module.
Synthetic module names derived from paths normalize period characters in path segments so fallback imports do not create invalid or misleading module hierarchies.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest runs with --import-mode=importlib against an installed package module that is reachable through normal imports, it should load that module under its canonical package-qualified name.

When --doctest-modules is used with a src-layout project whose package is installed non-editably, doctest collection should succeed without depending on a path-derived duplicate import of the same package module.
When consider_namespace_packages is enabled and the target module belongs to a namespace package, pytest should resolve and import it using the full namespace-qualified module name.

When a collected Python file is outside the normal import path, pytest should still import and collect it in importlib mode by falling back to a synthetic standalone module name without changing sys.path.
When the fallback synthetic name is derived from a path containing period characters in directory names, the resulting module identity should remain valid and not imply incorrect package nesting.
When pytest encounters the same module path again under the same resolved module identity, it should reuse the existing module object rather than importing it a second time.

task_7.title: Support Python 3.12 post-mortem debugging via sys.last_exc
task_7.description: The upgrade adds Python 3.12+ support for exposing the most recent test-call exception through sys.last_exc during pytest failure handling, while preserving the existing legacy post-mortem exception state used for debugging.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest exposes the latest test-call failure through Python 3.12's post-mortem debugging state so developers can inspect recent exceptions consistently after a failed test.

expectation.grounded: During pytest test-call execution, pytest should clear any previously stored post-mortem exception state before the call begins, including sys.last_exc when running on Python 3.12 or newer. If the test call raises an exception, pytest should populate sys.last_exc on Python 3.12+ in addition to continuing to set sys.last_type, sys.last_value, and sys.last_traceback for post-mortem debugging.
expectation.conceptual: On Python 3.12 and newer, a failed pytest test should make the most recent exception available through the standard sys.last_exc debugging hook, while keeping existing post-mortem exception information available in the usual way.

constraints.grounded: The change must preserve the existing behavior of sys.last_type, sys.last_value, and sys.last_traceback for failing test calls. Access to sys.last_exc must be conditional on Python versions where that attribute exists, so older Python versions continue to run without new attribute errors or changed failure semantics.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve debugger-visible exception state on newer Python versions without changing established failure reporting behavior or reducing compatibility on older supported runtimes.

behavior: Before running a test call, pytest clears previously stored post-mortem exception globals, including sys.last_exc on Python 3.12+ when present.
When a test call raises an exception, pytest stores that exception in sys.last_exc on Python 3.12+ for post-mortem debugging.
When a test call raises an exception, pytest continues to update sys.last_type, sys.last_value, and sys.last_traceback as part of its existing post-mortem debugging state.
On Python versions earlier than 3.12, pytest does not require or manipulate sys.last_exc and retains prior behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest runs a test call on Python 3.12 or newer, it should not leave a stale sys.last_exc value from an earlier failure in place before the new call begins.
When a test call fails on Python 3.12 or newer, the raised exception should be available afterward through sys.last_exc for post-mortem debugging.
When a test call fails on any supported Python version, sys.last_type, sys.last_value, and sys.last_traceback should still reflect the latest failure.
When pytest runs on Python versions older than 3.12, test execution and failure handling should continue without depending on sys.last_exc.

task_9.title: Support configurable append mode for pytest log files
task_9.description: Pytest's logging plugin now lets users choose whether file logging overwrites or appends to an existing log file. The new configuration applies both to the initially configured log file and to log files selected later through log path redirection, while preserving the previous overwrite behavior by default.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can configure pytest file logging to append to an existing log file instead of always truncating it, while preserving overwrite behavior as the default and applying the same mode when the log file path is changed during execution.

expectation.grounded: The logging plugin must expose `--log-file-mode` and `log_file_mode` as public configuration for file logging, accept only `w` or `a`, and default to `w`. `LoggingPlugin` must open the configured `log_file` and any later destination selected through `LoggingPlugin.set_log_path()` using the configured mode, so append mode preserves existing file contents and overwrite mode truncates them. Invalid mode values must be rejected during configuration parsing instead of being silently accepted.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to choose whether pytest replaces or appends to log-file contents. If append mode is selected, existing content in the target log file should remain and new log output should be added after it, including when pytest switches to a different log file during the run.

constraints.grounded: Keep overwrite mode as the default when no file mode is configured. Limit accepted file modes to the supported text modes `w` and `a`, and apply the selected mode consistently for both command-line and ini-based configuration, for initial log file opening, and for later log path updates.
constraints.conceptual: The change must stay backward compatible by preserving current overwrite behavior unless users explicitly opt into append mode. Mode handling should be validated and consistent regardless of where the log-file configuration comes from or whether the log destination changes later.

behavior: Pytest file logging now has a configurable file-open mode through `--log-file-mode` and `log_file_mode`.
The supported file-open modes are `w` for overwrite/truncate and `a` for append, with `w` remaining the default.
When append mode is configured, pytest preserves existing contents in the target log file and writes new log records after the existing content.
When overwrite mode is used, pytest continues to truncate the target log file before writing logs.
When `LoggingPlugin.set_log_path()` changes the active log file, the replacement file is opened with the same configured mode rather than always forcing overwrite mode.
Unsupported `log_file_mode` values are rejected as invalid configuration input.
acceptance_criteria: When a user configures `--log-file` without specifying a file mode, pytest should continue opening the log file in overwrite mode.
When a user sets `--log-file-mode=a` together with `--log-file`, pytest should retain any pre-existing content in that file and append newly emitted log entries after it.
When a user sets `log_file_mode = a` in configuration, pytest should append to the configured log file with the same observable behavior as the CLI option.
When pytest redirects file logging through `LoggingPlugin.set_log_path()`, it should open the new destination using the configured file mode rather than reverting to overwrite-only behavior.
When a user supplies a `log_file_mode` value other than `w` or `a`, pytest should reject the configuration instead of proceeding with logging.

task_8.title: Recognize bare pyproject.toml as a rootdir fallback
task_8.description: Pytest configuration discovery now treats a pyproject.toml file as the project config anchor for rootdir selection even when it does not contain pytest options, but only after no other suitable pytest configuration file has been found.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest can use a pyproject.toml file to establish the project root when no other supported pytest configuration file is found, even if the file does not define [tool.pytest.ini_options].

expectation.grounded: During config discovery, pytest should continue preferring any suitable supported pytest config file over pyproject.toml fallback behavior. If discovery finds a pyproject.toml but loadable pytest options are absent and no other suitable config is found, pytest should still treat that pyproject.toml as the discovered config location, set rootdir to its parent directory, expose that file as inipath, and leave the parsed ini configuration empty. When invoked without non-option path arguments, discovery should start from the invocation directory.
expectation.conceptual: Pytest should recognize a standard Python project rooted by pyproject.toml even when that file does not contain pytest-specific settings. This fallback should only influence project root detection when nothing more specific is available, and it must not change the existing precedence of normal pytest configuration files.

constraints.grounded: A bare pyproject.toml must not override a suitable pytest.ini, .pytest.ini, tox.ini, setup.cfg, or a pyproject.toml that provides pytest configuration. The fallback selection should not synthesize ini option values beyond choosing inipath and rootdir.
constraints.conceptual: Existing config-file precedence must remain stable, and the new fallback should only supply project-root discovery rather than inventing configuration settings.

behavior: If no suitable pytest configuration is found, a discovered pyproject.toml without pytest ini options should still be selected as the config anchor and define rootdir from its parent directory.
If multiple fallback-only pyproject.toml files are encountered during upward discovery, pytest should keep the closest one in the search order.
If a suitable pytest configuration file is found, it should take precedence over any previously seen bare pyproject.toml fallback candidate.
If pytest is run without non-option path arguments, config discovery should begin from the invocation directory.
acceptance_criteria: When a project contains only a pyproject.toml and no other supported pytest config file, running pytest should use that file's directory as rootdir even if the file has no [tool.pytest.ini_options] table.

When pytest discovers a pyproject.toml without pytest options in a nested project and no higher-priority config exists, it should report that pyproject.toml as the selected config location and keep ini options empty.

When multiple pyproject.toml files without pytest options exist on the search path and no other supported config is found, running pytest from the deepest location should select the nearest pyproject.toml.
When both a bare pyproject.toml and a suitable supported pytest config file are discoverable, pytest should use the supported pytest config file instead of the bare pyproject.toml fallback.

task_10.title: Report all fixture teardown errors
task_10.description: Pytest 8.1.1 changes fixture teardown error reporting so that if multiple fixture finalizers fail, all of those failures are surfaced together instead of only the first one being visible. This preserves the previous single-error behavior while improving teardown diagnostics for multi-failure cleanup paths.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that fixture teardown reports every exception raised by multiple finalizers for the same fixture, instead of surfacing only the first teardown failure.

expectation.grounded: During fixture teardown, pytest should execute all registered finalizers for the fixture even if earlier finalizers fail. If more than one finalizer raises, pytest should raise a grouped teardown exception via BaseExceptionGroup or ExceptionGroup containing all captured finalizer exceptions for that fixture. If exactly one finalizer raises, pytest should raise that original exception directly. After finalizer execution, pytest should still run the pytest_fixture_post_finalizer hook and clear cached fixture teardown state.
expectation.conceptual: When several cleanup callbacks fail while tearing down one fixture, users should see one aggregated teardown failure that exposes every underlying error. When only one cleanup callback fails, the visible behavior should remain a normal single exception.

constraints.grounded: Do not stop fixture finalization after the first teardown exception; remaining finalizers for the same fixture must still run. Do not introduce grouped exceptions for zero-failure or single-failure teardown cases. Successful teardown behavior outside this reporting change should remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The change should only expand teardown error visibility for multi-failure cases. It must not alter normal successful cleanup, and it must not make single teardown failures look different from before.

behavior: Fixture teardown continues running all registered finalizers even if one of them raises an exception.
If multiple finalizers for the same fixture raise during teardown, pytest reports them as one grouped teardown failure containing each underlying exception.
If exactly one finalizer raises during teardown, pytest preserves the prior behavior and surfaces that original exception directly.
After fixture teardown processing, pytest still performs post-finalizer hook notification and clears cached fixture teardown state.
acceptance_criteria: When two or more finalizers attached to the same fixture fail during teardown, the session should report one grouped teardown error that includes each individual finalizer exception.
When exactly one finalizer for a fixture fails during teardown, the reported failure should be that original exception rather than a grouped exception.
When one finalizer fails and later finalizers for the same fixture also fail, those later teardown failures should still be executed and included in the reported result.
When no finalizer fails during teardown, fixture cleanup should complete without introducing new teardown errors.
After fixture teardown runs, post-finalizer processing and fixture cleanup state invalidation should still occur.

task_11.title: Fix duplicate imports in pytest importlib mode
task_11.description: Pytest 8.1.1 fixes a regression in `--import-mode=importlib` so package-backed modules are resolved by their canonical import name when possible, preventing duplicate execution of non-test modules in scenarios such as installed packages, `src/` layouts, doctest collection, and namespace-package-aware imports while preserving isolated fallback imports for standalone test files.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that running pytest with `--import-mode=importlib` does not import the same non-test module more than once and resolves package-backed modules by their real module name, including projects that use `src/` layouts, doctest collection, installed packages, and optional namespace-package handling.

expectation.grounded: When pytest imports a module through `import_path` in `ImportMode.importlib`, it should first resolve the package root and canonical dotted module name, honoring `consider_namespace_packages` when enabled. If that canonical module is already loaded, pytest should reuse the existing module object instead of importing it again. If canonical package resolution succeeds, the module should be imported under that canonical name; if it does not, pytest should fall back to a unique path-derived module name. Generated fallback module names should normalize `.` characters in path segments so they remain valid module identifiers.
expectation.conceptual: With `--import-mode=importlib`, pytest should behave like normal Python importing for modules that belong to a real package, so doctest and collection do not execute the same application module twice. Files that are not importable through the active package path should still load as isolated modules without colliding with one another.

constraints.grounded: Preserve `importlib` mode support for distinct same-named test files in different directories, keep fallback imports working for files outside any resolvable package, and retain namespace-package-aware resolution only when `consider_namespace_packages` is enabled. Do not change the observable contract that unresolved files can still be imported via generated unique names.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must avoid duplicate imports without breaking existing support for isolated test modules, repeated imports of the same module, or projects that rely on namespace-package discovery. Package modules should keep their canonical identity, while standalone files should remain importable in a predictable, collision-safe way.

behavior: `--import-mode=importlib` now attempts to resolve a file's package root and canonical dotted module name before using a synthetic name derived from its path.
If the canonical module name is already loaded, pytest reuses the existing module object instead of importing the file a second time.
Modules that are reachable through normal package resolution are imported under their canonical package name rather than a root-relative synthetic name.
Files that cannot be resolved as part of a package continue to be imported as isolated modules using generated unique names.
Fallback-generated module names now normalize `.` characters in path segments to valid module-name characters so unusual directory names do not create invalid or misleading import names.
Canonical-name resolution can extend across namespace-package roots when namespace-package consideration is enabled.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest runs with `--import-mode=importlib` and encounters a package-backed module multiple times, it should reuse the same loaded module identity instead of re-executing that module.

When `--doctest-modules` is used with a `src/` layout against an installed package, pytest should resolve the doctested module by its actual package name rather than treating `src` as part of the module path.
When a Python file is importable as part of an installed or otherwise resolvable package, pytest should expose it under that canonical dotted module name.

When two same-named test modules exist in different directories that are not importable packages, `--import-mode=importlib` should still load them as distinct isolated modules without name collisions.
When fallback module names are derived from paths containing `.` within directory names, the resulting import should still succeed with a valid synthesized module identity.
When namespace-package handling is enabled, package resolution should recognize the namespace-package root instead of unnecessarily treating the file as a standalone module.

task_12.title: Limit --pyargs collection to the resolved package hierarchy
task_12.description: Pytest 8.1.1 fixes a regression introduced in 8.0.x where collecting tests via --pyargs could walk unrelated parent directories above the resolved package location. The upgrade restores a tighter collection tree for import-based targets, preventing avoidable permission-related collection failures while preserving normal path-based collection behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that invoking pytest with --pyargs against an importable package or module collects only within the resolved package hierarchy, so collection does not traverse unrelated parent directories and fail because of inaccessible ancestors.

expectation.grounded: When pytest resolves a --pyargs argument to an importable module or package, it should keep using the resolved filesystem target for collection while limiting parent collectors to the package ancestors implied by the original dotted module name. Explicit :: selection parts must continue to apply to the resolved target. Ordinary filesystem arguments must keep their existing confcutdir-based parent handling.
expectation.conceptual: --pyargs should behave like targeting an installed Python package, not like recursively walking arbitrary directories above that package. Users should be able to collect importable test targets without pytest exploring unrelated ancestors or failing because one of those unrelated directories is unreadable.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the behavior of collection arguments that do not use --pyargs, absolute path handling, directory validation, or :: selector parsing. Keep the fix scoped to parent-tree construction for successfully resolved --pyargs targets; other permission-related collection scenarios remain out of scope, and unresolved targets should continue to follow existing invalid-target failure behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The change must be narrowly scoped to import-based collection. Normal path-based discovery and existing error behavior for invalid targets should remain consistent, and the upgrade should not broaden collection beyond the requested module or package.

behavior: Pytest now distinguishes between regular path arguments and --pyargs arguments that were successfully resolved through the import path.
For resolved --pyargs targets, the collection tree includes only parent packages that match the dotted module hierarchy, and it stops before unrelated filesystem ancestors.
For ordinary path arguments, parent collection continues to be built from the path upward only while remaining within confcutdir.
Explicit :: node selection parts remain attached to the resolved collection target for both filesystem and --pyargs arguments.
If a --pyargs target cannot be resolved as an import-backed module or package, pytest keeps the existing missing-target failure semantics instead of treating it as a valid import hierarchy.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs pytest with --pyargs against an importable test module or package, the reported collection tree should begin at the resolved package root for that target and should not include unrelated parent directories above it.
When directories above the resolved package hierarchy are inaccessible, collecting the same importable --pyargs target should still succeed as long as the target itself is importable and accessible.
When a --pyargs target includes :: selectors, pytest should apply those selectors to the resolved module or package without changing selector behavior.
When pytest is invoked with normal filesystem paths instead of --pyargs, path-based collection ancestry should continue to follow existing confcutdir behavior.

task_15.title: Prevent duplicate Windows collection for tmp_path tests
task_15.description: The upgrade fixes a Windows-only pytest collection regression introduced in 8.0.2 where tests created under the tmp_path fixture could be collected multiple times when the same location was reachable through different filesystem aliases or symlink-like paths. The matcher now distinguishes true short-path equivalence from link-based aliases so a file is collected only once.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that on Windows, tests created with `tmp_path` are collected exactly once even when the same filesystem location can be referenced through alternate aliases or symlink-like paths.

expectation.grounded: When pytest resolves collection targets on Windows, path matching must continue to recognize equivalent paths that refer to the same file, but it must not treat a symlinked or linked alias as the same collection node as the non-link path. As a result, tests under `tmp_path` should no longer be collected multiple times because of alternate path representations while preserving short-path compatibility.
expectation.conceptual: Pytest should deduplicate collection for temporary test files on Windows correctly: genuine path aliases to the same non-linked file should still work, but linked aliases must not cause the same tests to appear more than once.

constraints.grounded: Maintain Windows support for matching equivalent filesystem paths that resolve to the same file. Do not regress collection behavior for valid same-file comparisons; only prevent matches that cross link status boundaries and would duplicate the same collected node.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing Windows path compatibility intact while blocking duplicate discovery caused by alternate linked views of the same location.

behavior: On Windows, collection path comparison still treats two paths as equivalent when they resolve to the same file.
A same-file match is no longer sufficient by itself if one path is a link and the other is not.
Tests located in directories created through `tmp_path` are no longer collected multiple times via alternate alias or symlink-like paths in CI environments.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest collects tests from a `tmp_path`-created location on Windows, it should report each discovered test once even if the directory also has an alternate alias path.
When two Windows paths refer to the same underlying non-linked file, collection should still treat them as the same target rather than failing to match them.
When one Windows path is a linked alias of the other, pytest should not merge them in a way that causes duplicate collection of the same test node.

task_14.title: Report marked-fixture warnings at the user fixture declaration
task_14.description: The upgrade fixes how pytest reports the deprecation warning for marks applied to fixtures. The warning still indicates that fixture marks have no effect, but it now points to the user-written fixture decorator location instead of pytest internals, making the warning actionable.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when a `pytest.mark.*` decorator is applied to a fixture, pytest reports the deprecation warning at the user’s fixture declaration so developers can identify and remove ineffective marks.

expectation.grounded: When a `pytest.mark.*` `MarkDecorator` is applied to a fixture function, pytest should continue to emit the existing marked-fixture deprecation warning (`PytestRemovedIn9Warning`) and attribute that warning to the external decorator call site in user code rather than to pytest’s internal mark storage machinery. Mark application for supported targets such as test functions and test classes should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Applying a pytest mark to a fixture should still warn that the mark has no effect, but the warning should highlight the fixture definition line that the user needs to fix. Normal use of marks on tests should behave the same as before.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove, rename, or broaden the marked-fixture deprecation condition. Do not change the warning category for this case. Do not change successful mark attachment behavior for test functions or test classes. The intended change is limited to the reported origin of the warning for fixture-mark misuse.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the same deprecation semantics and unaffected marking behavior elsewhere; only improve where the warning is reported so it points to the user-visible source of the issue.

behavior: Decorating a fixture with any `pytest.mark.*` mark continues to emit the existing deprecation warning that marks on fixtures have no effect.
The warning’s reported source location is the user code line where the fixture mark decorator is written, rather than an internal pytest frame.
Using `pytest.mark.*` on supported targets such as test functions or test classes continues to apply the mark without introducing this fixture-specific warning.
acceptance_criteria: When a fixture is decorated with a `pytest.mark.*` decorator, pytest should emit the existing marked-fixture deprecation warning during execution.
When that warning is displayed, its filename and line reference should identify the fixture’s decorator location in user code.

When a `pytest.mark.*` decorator is applied to a test function or test class, pytest should continue to attach the mark normally and should not emit the marked-fixture deprecation warning for that usage.

task_13.title: Restore xunit setup hooks under doctest-enabled collection
task_13.description: Upgrading from 8.0.2 to 8.1.1 restores xunit-style setup and teardown behavior when `--doctest-modules` is enabled, fixing a regression that could skip module initialization and leave collected tests running against uninitialized state.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that enabling `--doctest-modules` does not suppress xunit-style setup and teardown hooks, especially `setup_module`, so modules collected in doctest-enabled runs are initialized and cleaned up the same way as in normal pytest collection.

expectation.grounded: When pytest collects a module with `--doctest-modules`, recognized xunit-style hooks such as `setUpModule`/`setup_module` and `tearDownModule`/`teardown_module` must be discovered and executed automatically for that module. The same lifecycle registration must continue to cover `setup_function`/`teardown_function`, `setup_class`/`teardown_class`, and `setup_method`/`teardown_method`, with each hook running around the matching module, function, class, or method scope and receiving the corresponding collected object context.
expectation.conceptual: Doctest-enabled collection must preserve the legacy xunit lifecycle that users already rely on. Projects that initialize shared state in module-, function-, class-, or method-level setup hooks should see the same before-and-after behavior whether or not doctest collection is turned on.

constraints.grounded: Only pytest-recognized xunit hook names for module, function, class, and method scopes should participate in this automatic lifecycle. Restoring this behavior must not require users to rewrite those hooks as explicit fixtures, and hook execution must remain limited to the appropriate collection scope.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should restore consistency across collection modes without expanding the feature beyond established xunit behavior. Users should not need new configuration or manual workarounds to keep existing setup and teardown patterns functioning.

behavior: Running pytest with `--doctest-modules` executes `setup_module` or `setUpModule` before other collected items in the module rely on module-level state.
When present, `teardown_module` or `tearDownModule` runs after the module-scoped work finishes in a doctest-enabled run.
Function-level xunit hooks continue to run automatically around individual test functions, using the current collected function as context.
Class-level and method-level xunit hooks continue to run automatically around collected test classes and instance methods, using the corresponding class or method context.
Autouse lifecycle handling remains available during doctest module collection instead of being skipped because of the alternate collection path.
acceptance_criteria: When a module defines `setup_module` that changes module state and pytest is run with `--doctest-modules`, collected tests in that module should observe the initialized state.
When a module defines matching module teardown hooks, a doctest-enabled run should still execute them after the module scope completes.
When a project uses xunit-style function, class, or method setup and teardown hooks, enabling doctest collection should preserve their normal before-and-after execution around the relevant scope.
When users upgrade to 8.1.1, they should not need to replace existing xunit hooks with explicit fixtures just to recover correct initialization behavior under doctest-enabled collection.

task_16.title: Clarify tmp_path and tmpdir concurrency and retention behavior
task_16.description: The upgrade clarifies the documented contract for pytest temporary-directory fixtures. It explains that retained temporary directories are organized per test session, that retention is configurable, and that the same test run concurrently in separate pytest invocations can collide unless a distinct base temp location is provided.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the temporary-directory fixture documentation clearly explains how `tmp_path` and legacy `tmpdir` choose and retain their base directories, and that uniqueness applies per test function within a pytest invocation rather than across concurrent invocations of the same test.

expectation.grounded: The public documentation and fixture help text for `tmp_path` and legacy `tmpdir` should describe that pytest creates a new base temporary directory for each test session, retains prior base directories according to `tmp_path_retention_count` and `tmp_path_retention_policy`, and clears the base directory on each session when `--basetemp` is supplied. The documented behavior should also make clear that concurrent pytest invocations running the same test function are not guaranteed isolated temporary directories unless they use distinct base temp locations or prefixes.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to understand when temporary directories are isolated, when they are retained, and when concurrent runs can share or clash. The docs should set the expectation that default isolation is session-scoped, not a guarantee across separate concurrent pytest processes.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable runtime behavior of `tmp_path`, legacy `tmpdir`, or `--basetemp`. Preserve the existing retention controls and the existing behavior that `--basetemp` is cleared each session; this update only clarifies the documented contract and related references.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade should improve clarity without changing how temporary directories are created, retained, or cleared in actual test runs.

behavior: The documented contract for `tmp_path` states that each test session receives a new base temporary directory and older base directories may be retained for debugging according to the configured retention settings.
The documented contract for legacy `tmpdir` mirrors the same session-level base-directory retention and `--basetemp` clearing behavior.

The documentation clarifies that uniqueness of fixture-provided temporary directories does not extend across separate concurrent pytest invocations running the same test function unless distinct base temp locations are configured.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads the `tmp_path` fixture documentation, it should clearly state that base temporary directories are created per pytest session and retained according to the configured retention policy and count.
When a user reads the legacy `tmpdir` documentation, it should communicate the same retention and base-directory behavior as `tmp_path`.
When a user relies on `--basetemp`, the documentation should state that the specified base directory is cleared for each session.

When a user runs the same test concurrently in separate pytest invocations, the documented behavior should make it clear that fixture temp directories can clash unless separate base temp locations or prefixes are used.

task_18.title: Restore legacy path API compatibility until pytest 9.0
task_18.description: Pytest 8.1.1 rolls back an unintended 8.1.0 compatibility break for legacy path-based plugin APIs. Node constructors that still use `fspath` and hooks that still use `py.path.local` path arguments remain supported in 8.x, but now warn as removals deferred to pytest 9.0.0 rather than behaving as already removed in the 8.x line.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to pytest 8.1.1 does not break plugins or integrations that still rely on legacy path-based APIs, while clearly signaling that these interfaces are still deprecated and must be migrated before pytest 9.0.0.

expectation.grounded: Pytest must continue accepting the deprecated `fspath: py.path.local` argument for `Node` constructors and deprecated `py.path.local` hook path arguments in 8.1.1. These usages should emit deprecation warnings categorized for removal in pytest 9.0.0 via `PytestRemovedIn9Warning`, not fail as if removal already happened in the 8.x series. The public warning surface should no longer depend on `PytestRemovedIn8Warning`, and pytest should not automatically escalate `PytestRemovedIn9Warning` to errors by default in this release.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should preserve backward compatibility for older plugins that still use legacy path objects throughout the pytest 8.x line, while continuing to warn that those interfaces are on a removal path for pytest 9.0.0.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove runtime support for legacy `fspath` node-constructor usage or legacy `py.path.local` hook arguments in pytest 8.1.1. Do not make the deferred removal warnings hard failures by default. Deprecation signaling for these path-related APIs must remain observable and must target pytest 9.0.0 semantics.
constraints.conceptual: Maintain compatibility in the current major version, keep the deprecation visible, and avoid turning this deferred migration into an immediate runtime break.

behavior: Custom node construction that still passes `fspath: py.path.local` remains accepted in pytest 8.1.1 and produces a deprecation warning for removal in pytest 9.0.0.
Hook usage that still relies on legacy `py.path.local` path arguments remains accepted in pytest 8.1.1 and produces a deprecation warning for removal in pytest 9.0.0.
The warning category associated with these deferred removals is `PytestRemovedIn9Warning` rather than `PytestRemovedIn8Warning`.
Pytest no longer treats the deferred removal warning category as an error by default during normal warning capture in this release.
Consumers of pytest's public warning API should treat `PytestRemovedIn9Warning` as the relevant removal-warning class for these legacy path deprecations.
acceptance_criteria: When a plugin constructs a pytest node using the deprecated `fspath` argument, it should continue to run on pytest 8.1.1 and should emit a deprecation warning indicating removal is deferred to pytest 9.0.0.
When a plugin hook still uses legacy `py.path.local` path arguments, pytest 8.1.1 should continue operating and should emit a deprecation warning instead of failing because the argument was removed.
When code observes or filters the removal warning for these path-related deprecations, the relevant public warning category should be `PytestRemovedIn9Warning`.
When running under default warning handling in pytest 8.1.1, these deferred-removal warnings should remain warnings rather than becoming hard errors solely due to pytest's built-in warning policy.

task_17.title: Match fixture visibility against the real node hierarchy
task_17.description: Pytest 8.1.1 changes fixture discovery to use the actual collection tree instead of textual node ID parsing, which fixes package-scoped and autouse fixture visibility in edge cases such as packages collected from the project root. The update also changes private fixture-manager helper signatures to accept a Node object and removes a private node-id traversal helper used by some plugins.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that fixture lookup and autouse fixture application follow pytest's actual collection hierarchy rather than textual node ID parsing, so package- and directory-level fixtures remain visible to descendant tests even in edge-case layouts. Ensure that plugins or integrations using pytest's private fixture-resolution helpers remain compatible with the updated Node-based inputs and the removal of the private parent-nodeid iterator.

expectation.grounded: FixtureManager.getfixturedefs() and FixtureManager._getautousenames() should operate on a requesting Node, not a nodeid string, and should determine applicability from that Node's ancestor chain. Fixture matching should use the node hierarchy exposed by parent traversal, including for dynamic fixture lookup and fixture-availability reporting. Package-scope resolution should locate the matching Package ancestor by node identity and nodeid, and otherwise fall back to the session node. The private _pytest.nodes.iterparentnodeids() helper is no longer available.
expectation.conceptual: Fixture visibility should be determined from the real collected parent/child structure, not from string prefixes of node IDs. As a result, autouse fixtures and explicitly requested fixtures defined on packages or other ancestors should apply consistently to descendant tests, including unusual root-level package layouts. Integrations that depended on private helper APIs should treat this upgrade as a compatibility change.

constraints.grounded: Do not change normal fixture semantics beyond replacing textual ancestry checks with actual Node ancestry checks. Fixtures with global visibility should remain globally discoverable, unresolved fixture names should still report as missing, and package-scope lookup should still fall back to the session when no matching Package ancestor exists. No replacement private iterator for parent nodeids is introduced by this update.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should preserve existing fixture behavior except where prior string-based ancestry logic was incorrect. Global fixtures and ordinary missing-fixture behavior should continue to work as before, while incorrect exclusions caused by node ID text parsing should be eliminated.

behavior: FixtureManager.getfixturedefs(argname, node) now resolves applicable fixture definitions from the requesting Node and its ancestors instead of accepting a nodeid string.
FixtureManager._getautousenames(node) now derives autouse fixtures from the Node chain, so autouse applicability follows the actual collection hierarchy.

Fixture applicability is computed from ancestor Node.nodeid values obtained by traversing the real parent hierarchy, which fixes cases where textual nodeid parsing did not reflect the true parent relationship.

Dynamic fixture lookup and fixture-availability filtering use the requesting Node or its parent Node for applicability checks, aligning error reporting and late fixture resolution with the new hierarchy-based matching.
Package-scope fixture resolution searches ancestor Package nodes directly and falls back to the session node when no matching package ancestor is present.
The private _pytest.nodes.iterparentnodeids() helper has been removed, so callers can no longer rely on that function being present.
acceptance_criteria: When a test item requests a fixture, pytest should consider fixture definitions attached to actual ancestor collectors of that item, even if those ancestors are not textual prefixes of the item's node ID.
When autouse fixtures are declared on a package, directory, or other ancestor collector, descendant tests should receive those fixtures according to the real collection tree.

When a package-scoped fixture is resolved for an item under a matching Package collector, pytest should bind that scope to the matching Package; when no such Package ancestor exists, it should fall back to the session scope.
When a plugin or integration calls FixtureManager.getfixturedefs() or FixtureManager._getautousenames(), it should pass a Node object rather than a nodeid string.
When a plugin or integration depends on _pytest.nodes.iterparentnodeids(), it should no longer expect that private helper to exist in pytest 8.1.1.
